content_voiceover: This table makes a point that's easy to forget on boards, that a negative day forty-two minimal residual disease result doesn't mean the same thing in every patient. Among patients who were M R D negative at day forty-two, those with favorable genotypes, like hyperdiploid or E T V six colon colon R U N X one, had a cumulative relapse risk of just one point three percent. But patients with intermediate or unfavorable genotypes, including P A X five alt, M E F two D rearranged, E T V six colon colon R U N X one like, T cell ALL, i AMP twenty-one, B C R colon colon A B L one, B C R colon colon A B L one like, and K M T two A rearranged, had a relapse risk of nine point five percent, even though their day forty-two M R D was also negative. That's roughly a seven-fold difference, and it's highly significant. The teaching point is that genetic subtype still matters for risk stratification even after you've cleared M R D, so a negative M R D result in a high-risk genotype should not be treated as reassuring as the same result in a favorable genotype.
keypoints: Day 42 MRD-negative does not equal equal risk across genotypes
Intermediate or unfavorable genotype MRD-negative: 9.5% relapse risk
